title: Hurricane Maria: Blue Roof Relief
description:
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers installs the first temporary Blue Roof on a home in Ponce; Puerto Rico's second largest city.

Anchor lead:
SURVIVING HURRICANE MARIA WAS JUST HALF THE BATTLE FOR THE RESIDENTS OF PUERTO RICO… NOW THEY'RE FOCUSING ON REBUILDING THEIR LIVES. THE U-S ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEER’S MIKE GLASCH SHOWS US HOW ONE OF USACE’S SIGNATURE DISASTER RECOVERY EFFORTS… THE BLUE ROOF PROGRAM... PROVIDES SOME MUCH NEEDED RELIEF TO THE PEOPLE OF THE DEVASTATED ISLAND.

Anchor tag:
THE DEADLINE TO APPLY FOR THE BLUE ROOF ROOF PROGRAM IN PUERTO RICO IS DECEMBER FOURTH.
keywords: Maria, Ponce, blue, Hurricane Maria, VIPR, USACE, engineers, Hurricane, roof
unit_name: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Omaha District

transcript.text: ^- [Mike] Since Hurricane Maria decimated Puerto Rico,
^the US Army Corps of Engineers has installed
^more than 4,000 temporary blue roofs.
It's estimated that there are 60,000 homes
throughout the island in need of this temporary fix.
This house is the first home in Ponce,
Puerto Rico's second-largest city,
to have a blue roof installed.
^- We believe we are gonna lose everything,
^'cause the thing is, if we don't cover what we have,
^we're gonna lose it.
I know and I understand it's not easy,
but I said, "Wow, FEMA's around here."
We're gonna do...
With peace.
We're gonna have at least a little bit of peace.
Even though we don't have light,
but we could live without it.
But the thing is, if you lose
what you have inside your house,
then we're gonna be worse,
'cause it's not easy.
I'mma tell you, it's not.
- [Mike] To get residents in need signed up for the program,
a little bit of legwork had to be put in first.
^- For Puerto Rico, it was a little bit different.
^They don't really have a defined address system
^in some of the rural areas,
so we start going door-to-door.
We talk to the people in Puerto Rico.
We talk to the residents who have damaged homes.
We tell them about our program.
- [Mike] To be eligible for the Blue Roof Program,
the home must have less than 50% structural damage.
The temporary covering not only prevents
further damage to the property,
it also reduces temporary housing costs
by allowing residents to remain in their homes
while recovering from the storm.
But the biggest benefit of the program?
- Relief. They know that people are here to help them,
especially once they see the blue roofs
going on in their neighborhood.
They know that it's coming soon,
and they're grateful, and they're relieved.
We're here trying to help put people back in their homes,
gives them a place to call their home that they can
rebuild and start getting their lives back to normalcy.
Starting today here in Ponce, with this house right here.
- We feel a little bit peace
now that we're seeing you people around.
- [Mike] With roofs now going on in Ponce,
^the program will continue to expand throughout the island.
^Mike Glasch, US Army Corps of Engineers, Puerto Rico.
